weather_report:
Subiaco dozes under a hush of cloud before dawn, the air smelling faintly of wet stone. Light rain is set to arrive with first light and linger into the school-run hours, softening the edges of the morning and blurring streetlamps into halos. Sun will be shy at best early on; UV stays low beneath this blanket of grey, rising only if the cloud loosens later. Expect a muted, silvery start rather than sparkle, with visibility fine but the day’s clarity more watercolor than line drawing.

It looks quietly pleasant if you like the world slowed down. Dress for drizzle and cool air: a light waterproof or hooded layer, shoes that don’t mind puddles, and something you can shed if the skies brighten. If the rain keeps on, nurse a coffee by the window, take the early train instead of the bike, run a short errand between showers, or settle into those small, useful tasks that reward patience. Should the cloud thin toward late morning, step out for a gentle walk under damp plane trees, and tuck a little sunscreen in your pocket on the off chance the sun makes a brief, sharper appearance.
